clue.text: Husband on board poorly lit boat

indicators.note: something on board a ship is inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: dim and gloomy
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband sits aboard a badly lit boat at night.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside DINGY, between its G and Y, giving DINGHY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small open boat, often a sailing or rowing tender.

clue.text: Star of French cinema's first speech

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter only of the word it qualifies

parts.note: first letter of cinema
a formal speech

explanation.surface: A leading French film actor gives the opening address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a film star; here it is a military medal or order.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is an insignia of an order of knighthood or a medal, which is a decoration.

clue.text: New record a while ago with melody taken from 9

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
an EP, extended play, is a record format of an earlier era
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A fresh release of an old record, with its melody lifted from another work.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is PLANET, so 'taken from 9' means one example drawn from that class.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the eighth planet from the Sun, so it is one drawn from the set of planets.

clue.text: One would expect a player to behave appropriately

parts.words: One would expect a player to behave appropriately
parts.note: surface reading: a sportsman or actor ought to conduct himself well
setter's reading: a musician would be expected to play the correct pitch, the phrase also meaning to say or do just the right thing

explanation.surface: Players should be on their best behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests sport or acting, but it is a musician, for whom the idiom is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the right note is an idiom for saying or doing exactly what suits the occasion.

clue.text: Candour unwisely shown about large witches' pot

indicators.note: shown about means placed around, so the scrambled letters wrap round another piece
doing something unwisely suggests it goes wrong, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Speaking frankly at the wrong moment about a witches' big pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CANDOUR are rearranged around L to make CAULDRON.
explanation.definitionFit: A cauldron is the large cooking vessel witches stir in stories such as Macbeth.

clue.text: Language used when armchair almost collapsed

indicators.note: something collapsed has fallen in a heap, so its letters land in a new order
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming and rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone swore in a foreign tongue when the armchair nearly gave way.
explanation.walkthrough: ARMCHAIR loses its last letter to leave ARMCHAI, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Amharic is the official working language of Ethiopia, a Semitic tongue.

clue.text: Painter cooked vindaloo and rice

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist preparing a curry supper for himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Italian Renaissance artist who painted the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper.

clue.text: Revolutionary university in revolutionary broadcast

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the other piece

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary

indicators.note: a revolution is a turning round, so the word after it is read backwards

parts.note: Yale is a US Ivy League university

explanation.surface: A radical college's messages are transmitted by an insurgent station.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'revolutionary' does two jobs: first a turning signal, then a red.
explanation.definitionFit: Relayed means passed on or transmitted, as a broadcast signal is.

clue.text: Celebrity from Dublin, a megastar

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken straight out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: letters running across the end of Dublin, a and the start of megastar

explanation.surface: An Irish superstar from Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: A big name is a famous person, so name alone is a synonym for celebrity.

clue.text: Earth perhaps flat? Theory, initially

parts.note: a plane is a flat surface

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter only is kept

parts.note: first letter of Theory

explanation.surface: Questioning the flat-Earth theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth perhaps' signals an example: Earth is one of several.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is one instance of a planet, a body orbiting the Sun.

clue.text: Splendid Havana, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: excellent, in a dated British exclamation
second meaning: Havana is an example of a city that is the seat of government

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' is an old-fashioned British way of saying 'excellent!'; Havana is the capital of Cuba.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as a dated adjective for excellent and as a noun for a country's chief city, of which Havana is one.

clue.text: Person vandalising cowl on chimney

parts.note: a cowl is a monk's hood
lum is a Scottish and northern English word for chimney; on means placed after

explanation.surface: Someone damaging the cowl fitted on top of a chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: A chimney cowl is also a real metal cap on a flue, which helps the surface. LUM is Scots for chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodlum is a thug or hooligan, the kind of person who goes round vandalising property.

clue.text: Crude thug with money

parts.note: a rough is a violent hooligan
with means along with, and
the ready, or readies, is slang for cash

explanation.surface: A boorish heavy who happens to be loaded with cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Readies' is British slang for ready money, cash in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough-and-ready describes something crude or makeshift but serviceable.

clue.text: Very evil trap set up for game

parts.note: real is informal for very, as in real good

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means raised upwards, so the words are read from the bottom

parts.note: sin is wickedness
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A wicked trap laid ready to catch game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' tempts as quarry for the trap; it is the sport. Real tennis is the indoor original of tennis, played at Hampton Court.
explanation.definitionFit: Real tennis is the old court game from which lawn tennis developed.

clue.text: Who will have reviewed this Sheridan play?

parts.words: Who will have reviewed this Sheridan play?
parts.note: surface reading: asking which reviewer covered a Sheridan production
setter's reading: the person whose job is reviewing plays is also the title of a Sheridan comedy

explanation.surface: Wondering which theatre reviewer covered a revival of a Sheridan comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Brinsley Sheridan, the 18th-century playwright, wrote a satire on theatre named after the person who reviews plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The Critic (1779) is Sheridan's farce lampooning theatre, critics and rehearsals.

clue.text: Magistrate imprisoning duke for evasion

indicators.note: imprisoning means locking up inside, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A judge jailing an aristocrat for tax evasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Doge, the elected chief magistrate of the Venetian Republic, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a trick or ruse for evading something, so the noun matches evasion.

clue.text: Leader of opposing side is outstanding

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: first letter of opposing
a wing is one side of a team, building or political party

explanation.surface: The opposition party's leader stands out from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means not yet paid here, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding is still owing, unpaid and due.

clue.text: One from the Middle East is one king brought over

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: brought over suggests turned over, so the pieces before it are flipped round

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, and King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern monarch flown in for a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israeli is a citizen of Israel, a Middle Eastern country.

clue.text: Children's author had dollar exchanged

indicators.note: currency exchanged is changed into something else, so these letters are converted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A children's writer swapped a dollar at a bureau de change.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl wrote Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, Matilda and other children's books.

clue.text: Get near volatile chemical substance

indicators.note: volatile means unstable and liable to change, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning to approach an unstable chemical with care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volatile' fits the chemistry so well it reads as part of the definition, but it is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance used to cause or detect a chemical reaction.

clue.text: Article put in last, possibly at an angle

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so one piece goes inside the other
possibly suggests one arrangement out of several, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item filed at the end, possibly crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' could be A or THE; only AN supplies the N this answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means slanting or on a slope, so it sits at an angle.

clue.text: Complaint from the Italian chaps stationed in the outskirts of Aldershot

indicators.note: stationed in means posted inside, so the pieces are placed within the outer letters
outskirts are the edges of a town, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of Aldershot
il is Italian for the
chaps are men

explanation.surface: An Italian soldiers' grievance about being posted on the fringes of Aldershot.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldershot is a British Army garrison town in Hampshire, which suits 'stationed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness, which is an ailment.

clue.text: On what a local tax may be based in area A (but level fluctuates)

definitions.text: On what a local tax may be based

indicators.note: something that fluctuates keeps moving about, so the letters before it are shifted around

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Local tax bands vary by area, though the levels keep moving.
explanation.walkthrough: Rateable value was the notional rental value of a property on which British local rates were charged, before the council tax.
explanation.definitionFit: British domestic rates were calculated by multiplying a property's rateable value by a council's rate in the pound.

clue.text: Girl in form caught out

indicators.note: out means removed, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: a form is a school class
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl in a class was caught skipping lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a mainly northern British and Scottish word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Captain brought in an eastern perennial

indicators.note: brought in means taken inside, so one piece is placed within the others

parts.note: taken as written
Captain Nemo commands the Nautilus in Jules Verne's novels
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A ship's captain arrives with a plant from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Nemo is the commander of the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone is a flowering plant that returns year after year, so it is a perennial.

clue.text: Grandmother cutting a cotton cloth

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
keen means sharp, as of a cutting edge

explanation.surface: Granny busy cutting out a length of cotton fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like a verb for granny's sewing, but it is an adjective meaning sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton fabric originally made in Nanjing, China.

clue.text: Dagger found in street by messy toilet

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: something messy is in disorder, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A weapon turns up in the street beside a filthy public lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slender tapering blade.

clue.text: Opening bowler, perhaps American, catches one

indicators.note: a thing that catches another takes hold of it, so it closes around that piece

parts.note: a bowler is a kind of hat
I is the Roman numeral for one
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A cricket line-up with an American opening bowler taking a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening bowler' reads as cricket, but Opening is the definition and bowler is the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a gap or break, an opening in a sequence.
